acceptance.criterion: Parse and schema-validate the brief and verify evidence-backed component selection for every required function without relaxing the original requirements. Any unsupported selection remains an explicit failure or refusal, not acceptance.

Complete and verify electrical connectivity, supply and current budgets, signal compatibility, required decoupling and all supporting electrical/thermal calculations. Resolve every physical electrical binding and numerical requirement with evidence.
Verify the 45 by 30 mm maximum outline, cold-junction placement, terminal thermal region, input filtering and host interface routing.
Run actual fabrication DRC against named profile CYCLE5_2L_FR4_1OZ, resolving violations and checking the requested stackup and single-side assembly. A named profile is not a claim that DRC has run.

Generate and cross-check manufacturing outputs: copper/mask/silkscreen/outline fabrication layers, drill files, stackup/fabrication notes, BOM, placement file and assembly drawing, with mutually consistent revision and coordinates.

After at least 10 minutes equilibration in still air, exercise hot-junction equivalents 0, 100, 200 and 300 degC at terminal ambients 15, 25 and 35 degC using a calibrated floating thermocouple simulator and independently measured temperature of each copper transition. At each point require absolute measured error + fixture expanded uncertainty U (k=2) <=3 degC, with U<=0.5 degC. Establish an evidence-backed error bound between the discrete points throughout the full requested continuous ranges. Verify TC and CJ each acquire fresh samples >=4 Hz with <=250 ms intervals and <=100 ms effective timestamp skew in published pairs. Verify terminal-pair and sensor-to-EACH-terminal <=0.5 degC mismatch. No electrical or hardware success is pre-approved.

constraints.description: All numerical requirements and fixture choices are independent ENGINEERING_DEFAULT decisions, not manufacturer facts. No part selections are prescribed.
External fixture supplies only the stated power, stimulus, host and load. Required signal conversion and conditioning remain on this board.

Named fabrication DRC profile CYCLE5_2L_FR4_1OZ: minimum finished trace width 0.20 mm, copper clearance 0.20 mm, plated drill 0.30 mm, annular ring 0.15 mm and copper-to-routed-edge clearance 0.30 mm. These are independent prototype fabrication defaults, not an assertion of any manufacturer capability.

functions.description: Type K differential acquisition and cold-junction compensation
requirements: Accept one ungrounded Type K thermocouple through a two-terminal connector. Type K extension wire reaches the board terminals; transitions to board copper define the cold junction.

Core board hardware must acquire differential thermocouple voltage and physically sense the terminal cold-junction temperature. The host may perform documented Type K linearization and compensation arithmetic from board raw measurements; the host may not provide the cold-junction measurement.

Across the entire continuous hot-junction range 0 to 300 degC and terminal/board ambient range 15 to 35 degC, absolute board-indicated hot-junction error including conversion, linearization and cold-junction error shall not exceed 3 degC. Probe calibration and extension-wire inhomogeneity are excluded from board error and separately characterized. For each validation measurement, pass only if absolute measured error plus the fixture expanded uncertainty U (coverage factor k=2) is <=3 degC; U must be <=0.5 degC. Twelve specified discrete test points sample this continuous requirement but do not replace it; an evidence-backed between-point error bound is also required.

Operating hot-junction range is 0 to 300 degC and terminal/board ambient is 15 to 35 degC. Deliver genuinely new thermocouple samples at least four times per second and genuinely new cold-junction samples at least four times per second; each channel has at most 250 ms between fresh acquisitions. Each published measurement pair uses acquisitions whose effective sample timestamps differ by at most 100 ms. Repeating or re-labeling an old sample is not a fresh update.

Fixture has a floating thermocouple source, at most 100 ohm total loop resistance, at most 1 m unshielded twisted extension pair, no imposed common-mode voltage and no intentional RF disturbance. Provide input bias/return and filtering on board without relying on a grounded hot junction.

The two copper-transition terminal temperatures must differ by no more than 0.5 degC. The cold-junction sensor temperature must differ from EACH copper-transition temperature by no more than 0.5 degC, not merely their average, under the stated steady-state fixture. Locate the cold-junction sensor within 5 mm of the copper transition region; use an isothermal placement region away from dissipative circuitry.
No galvanic isolation, hazardous-voltage connection, open-wire diagnosis or probe supply is required.

requirements: Use SPI with separate chip select, clock, host-to-board data and board-to-host data at 3.3 V logic, clock no faster than 1 MHz. Document SPI mode, transaction format, sample units/scaling and freshness indication.
Host controls acquisition and reads measurements; a board processor is optional, but analog acquisition and cold-junction sensing cannot be external.

Digital fixture default: both host and board receivers shall recognize inputs <=0.8 V as low and >=2.0 V as high. Both host and board active outputs shall provide <=0.4 V low and >=2.8 V high at the specified load throughout the declared board supply range. These are compatibility requirements, not measured capabilities.

Each active digital output drives at most 0.5 mA steady-state load and 30 pF total load including receiver, connector and fixture wiring. Each receiver input leakage magnitude is <=10 uA. Output 10%-90% rise and fall times at that load must be between 2 ns and 20 ns. Fixture logic high never exceeds the instantaneous board supply.

Power sequence is controlled, not arbitrary: connect common ground first; power the host with its board-directed signals held low and board-output receivers high-impedance; apply board power, allow 100 ms settling, then start transactions/clocks. For shutdown stop clocks, drive host outputs low, remove board power, then remove host power. Board-output receivers remain powered and high-impedance until board power is removed. No connector signal may power an unpowered endpoint.
Firmware and fixture must prevent contention; the host never actively drives the board data-output pin. No hot-plug operation is required.
Mark positive and negative Type K polarity. Terminations and sensor placement form the board cold-junction region.

functions.description: Regulated external DC entry and board power distribution
requirements: Accept the declared external regulated supply at the power connector and distribute it with implementation-required local decoupling. Any internally derived rails and their budgets remain on-board responsibilities; the source is not a substitute for core signal conversion.

interfaces.description: External regulated 3.3 V supply and common return.
Common-ground SPI host; logic endpoints must be compatible throughout the supply range. External host outputs may not exceed board supply.
Floating Type K input; normal differential voltage envelope only, not a withstand rating. No intentional excitation; 1 uA maximum input current per lead.

manufacturing.note: No mandatory mounting holes; fixture supports board edges with insulated clips. Board dimensions include connectors, excluding mating cables.

sources.description: Regulated external DC supply; stated operating range applies at board connector.

summary: A compact non-isolated Type K thermocouple measurement board with on-board cold-junction sensing and a digital host interface.
